2_Introduction: The devices exhibited an increased PCE from 25.4599% to 25.4599%, with a VOC of 1.1852 V, FF of 83.7852%, and JSC of 25.638 mA/cm². The mixed perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) precursor solution was prepared with a total concentration of 1.65 mol/L in DMF/DMSO co-solvent. The deposition process involved a two-step spin sequence (1000 rpm/5 s and 6000 rpm/30 s) to achieve a controlled film thickness. A gentle antisolvent drop of 150 µL at last 15 s guided the perovskite crystals into a more ideal arrangement. The perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ benefits from A-site cation engineering, where the small Cs⁺ ion stabilizes the cubic α-phase and the FA⁺/MA⁺ mixture optimizes the tolerance factor, collectively suppressing phase segregation and mitigating ion migration. The crystallization was precisely controlled through a 1.65 M precursor in a DMF/DMSO co-solvent system, which stabilized the PbI₂·DMSO intermediate phase, followed by a two-step spin-coating sequence (1000 rpm/5 s and 6000 rpm/30 s) to establish a uniform liquid film and facilitate gradual solvent evaporation. The critical intervention of a gentle 150 µL antisolvent drip at 15 seconds before the spin cycle's end triggered a controlled supersaturation, guiding the nucleation and growth of perovskite crystals into a denser, more ideal arrangement with reduced pinhole density, while the subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes drove off residual solvents and completed the crystallization into a highly crystalline film with minimal intrinsic defects. This optimized processing sequence resulted in a champion device achieving a high open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.1852 V, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.638 mA/cm², a fill factor (FF) of 83.7852%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4599%.
